subject: Founders: mixed startup + education credit eligibility and baseline rate question
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <founders@lighthouselabs.org>

Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Eligibility for education+startup credits — quick clarity

Hi Soojin,

Hope you’re well. Quick question — Lighthouse Labs is a very early-stage incubator that runs cohort programs for undergrad and grad students. We’re incorporated as an LLC but run fee-waived cohorts for partner universities; a few of our projects are non-profit-led. We’re evaluating Redwood for chat + embeddings for a pilot starting July.

Two things I wanted to check before I get legal involved:
- Do you have a path for combined startup + education credits? Some of our student projects would be eligible for education discounts but the parent org is a for-profit.
- For baseline pricing: what’s the apply-able hosted-API rate for a pilot (monthly token volume estimate ~2M tokens) if we also take a $3k credit? Any documentation or a one-pager helps.

Attaching a short one-pager about Lighthouse Labs. Happy to hop on a 20-min call if easier.

Thanks,
Alex
Founder, Lighthouse Labs

Subject: Re: Eligibility for education+startup credits — quick clarity

Hi Alex — thanks for the note and the one-pager, that’s helpful context.

Short answer: we do have programs for academic cohorts and for early-stage startups, but combined eligibility depends on whether the program is run as an official university-affiliated offering or if the parent org is operating the cohort as a commercial product. We’ll need a couple of quick items to route an exception for a hybrid case:

1) A brief statement from your partner university confirming the cohorts are educational (email or letter).
2) If you want startup credits on top of education pricing, we need a short breakdown of which projects are commercial vs. nonprofit educational (just a table or bullet list).

Neha from pricing/finance is cc’d — can you advise on what a baseline pilot rate looks like for ~2M tokens/month and a $3k credit? Ben, looping you for any contractual notes re: MA terms.

If it helps, Alex — I can schedule a quick 20-min slot today or tomorrow to run through this and the approval path.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Alex Ramos <founders@lighthouselabs.org>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eligibility for education+startup credits — quick clarity

Thanks for the context. Quick pricing and process note from finance/discounts: 

- Baseline hosted API list rate (standard): $0.0008 per input token / $0.0012 per output token (example model family).
- Typical education pilot program: 50% off list for verified academic programs + up to $5k in onboarding credits for first 3 months.
- Typical startup credits: $3k-$10k credits based on YC/accelerator status or seed-stage evidence.

For hybrid requests where the legal entity is for-profit but cohorts are educational, we require:
  a) University confirmation (email from university domain or signed letter)
  b) A project-level mapping indicating which workloads are student/edu vs. commercial

If both a) and b) are submitted, we can approve an exception to stack education pricing (50% off) with a $3k startup promo credit for the broader org for the pilot period. Approval is by Sales Ops and requires a short MA amendment. Contractually we can do a six-month pilot with the following term we commonly offer: 50% off hosted token rates up to $5k/month equivalent spend (after credits), and the $3k promo applied to first invoice. 

I’ve attached a proposed MA terms doc for review. Ben — if this looks fine from legal/terms side we can issue a one-off pricing exception and prepare a DocuSign.

Neha Kapoor
Director, Pricing & Finance | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Proposed_MA_terms.docx (DOCX, 45KB)
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Alex Ramos <founders@lighthouselabs.org>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eligibility for education+startup credits — quick clarity

Hi all — quick confirmation from legal/contracting side: the MA amendment Neha drafted covers the stacking of academic pricing with a one-time startup promo credit. Two notes:

- We’ll need the university confirmation before executing the DocuSign link (helps with audit trail).
- The amendment includes an opt-out clause at 6 months and a clause that commercial projects will be reviewed for conversion to standard rates if they exceed the agreed pilot thresholds.

Alex — once you upload the university confirmation and the project mapping (can be a short Google Doc), I’ll issue a DocuSign link for signatures. I’ve added a standard clause to protect both sides; if you need edits, flag them and we’ll loop legal.

Best,
Ben Carter
